text:
Aisha: Heads up — customer acme-inc is seeing a sustained throughput sag on their Dedicated pool (pool:d-42) since ~09:15 PST. Ticket #4321. Multiple requests are getting high p95 latency and some 5xx errors. Escalating here.
Priya: Got it, joining. Any error samples or a repro from the customer?
Aisha: Pasting a minimal repro + observed logs. Customer traffic is a stream of very short prompts (~20-60 tokens) at ~120 qps. They switched a pipeline yesterday to chunked requests. Example request they sent:```curl -X POST "https://dedicated.redwood.ai/pool/d-42/v1/generate" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-acme..." \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rw-open-7b","input":"Summarize: hi"}'
```
And relevant runtime line from node logs:```[09:17:21.452] batcher.INFO pack_timeout_ms=25 max_batch_tokens=1024 tokens_in_batch=64 pack_size=1 prefill_tokens=48 infer_tokens=16```
Aisha: Also seeing retries in customer logs (401s for ~10s) around 09:16 that correlate with an auth refresh issue — they retried which increased thin bursts.
Marco: That batcher log screams micro-batches. pack_size=1 + tokens_in_batch low. Two quick hypotheses: (1) continuous-batcher is failing to coalesce requests because of token accounting (prefill vs infer) or very short pack_timeout, (2) scheduler config (max_batch_tokens or fair-queue weights) is preventing compatible requests from being combined.
Sam: Autoscaler kicked but scale didn't help throughput much. From infra: GPU utilization per replica is ~22% but thin_batch_rate is 61% and avg_pack_size=1.15. Autoscaler log:```[09:20] autoscaler.INFO pool:d-42 desired=6->8 reason=load spike``` then shortly after:```[09:23] autoscaler.INFO no_effect: thin_batching persists```.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: scale start for pool:d-42 at 09:20:05 (desired=6->8)
Priya: Can you share a short reproducer we can run on a canary pool? If we can repro locally we can iterate on pack_timeout/max_batch_tokens.
Aisha: Attaching a quick python loop reproducer the customer used:```# repro.py
import requests, time
url = 'https://dedicated.redwood.ai/pool/d-42/v1/generate'
for i in range(2000):
  requests.post(url, json={'model':'rw-open-7b','input':'x'}, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-acme'})
  time.sleep(0.02)```
Aisha: Customer also noted they flipped off kv-cache in their deploy yesterday (prefill_kv_cache=false) which I think forces a heavier prefill phase for many short prompts.
Marco: That can definitely do it. If prefill_tokens are large relative to infer_tokens, the scheduler may treat requests as incompatible because they inflate tokens_in_batch and hit max_batch_tokens quickly. Check pool config: `prefill_kv_cache=false`, `max_batch_tokens=1024`, `pack_timeout_ms=25`.
Sam: Also check fair-queue weights — looks like this tenant's requests are being isolated to a single scheduling lane due to priority settings in the pool, which amplifies pack starvation when their requests are tiny.
Priya: Quick mitigation options: (A) increase pack_timeout_ms (to 50-100ms) to allow more coalescing, (B) increase max_batch_tokens to 4096 for the pool so token accounting doesn't prematurely block packing, (C) enable kv_cache for that pool (prefill_kv_cache=true) so prefill cost is amortized, (D) route customer to an alt pool with different scheduler settings while we triage.
Marco: Also recommend instrumenting and measuring `thin_batch_rate`, `avg_pack_size`, and `prefill_ratio` before/after changes. I'll prepare a small canary change toggling pack_timeout and kv cache.
Priya: Running reproducer on canary now (canary:d-99). Will flip pack_timeout=75ms and kv_cache=true and post metrics in ~10m.
deploy-bot: canary deploy: update pool canary:d-99 pack_timeout_ms=75 prefill_kv_cache=true at 09:40:12
Aisha: Customer accepted temporary workaround — routing traffic to alt pool (pool:d-60) which has higher pack_timeout and kv_cache enabled. They see p95 down from ~1.8s to ~420ms after switch.
Marco: Long term we should reconcile config drift across pool versions: pool:d-42 had older scheduler/batcher defaults that mismatch our current model of prefill accounting. I'll open an infra task to audit pool defaults and add a diagnostic alert for thin_batch_rate>40%.
Sam: Also sanity-check autoscaler behavior: scaling more nodes won't help if pack_size stays ~1. We should add an autoscale hold when thin_batch_rate above threshold to avoid wasting replicas.
Aisha: Will update ticket #4321 with reproduction steps, mitigations we tried, and the customer's acceptance of pool reroute. Thanks all — Priya please paste canary numbers when ready and we can close the loop. :thumbsup:
